newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl eye joint drive for broader NATO.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl eye joint drive for broader NATO.

text.p: The leaders of France and Germany are discussing a joint initiative to enable Romania and Slovenia to join NATO from the start of enlargement despite U.S. objections, a French source said on Friday.

The source said President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl had discussed the idea after the United States said on Thursday it wanted to restrict the first wave of NATO expansion to three central European countries -- the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.

"The chancellor and the president will consider a joint proposal to allow Romania and one other country (Slovenia) to have their candidacies taken into account from the start at the Madrid NATO summit (on July 8 and 9)," the source said.

The source said the U.S. position, announced by the White House on Thursday despite widespread support among the European NATO allies for a broader enlargement, appeared to be dictated by the higher cost and concern in Congress over the budgetary implications.

France has been in the vanguard of European countries campaigning for Romania and Slovenia to be admitted, arguing that the move would show the alliance's concern for security in the Balkans, the Black Sea area and the Mediterranean.
Germany only came out publicly in favour of Romania and Slovenia at a meeting of European centrist parties this week.
